bios.title: Charlie Hane
paragraphs: Charlie Hane is a Los Angeles-based director, producer, and writer. In 2025, he began producing the feature documentary THE ETERNAL STEPPE, building it from scratch in Mongolia's remote steppe and leading a twelve-person international crew; it is now in post-production, with network distribution talks underway. That same year, he released DIVORCED DADS HOTEL, a short film he wrote, directed, edited, and starred in, and which won the IndieFEST Film Festival and International Independent Shorts Awards, plus a Cannes Indie Shorts Semi-Finalist nod. In 2026, he produced and assistant-directed MASHA/MARIA, a Dance on Camera Production Grant recipient that premiered at Film at Lincoln Center, shot with SCUBA cinematography in a blackout pool. That same year, he produced and assistant-directed the music video for Citizen's HALCYON BLUES (over 200 million Spotify streams), and creatively produced and animated the proof-of-concept pilot UP THE WATER SPOUT, which drew 500,000 Instagram views within 24 hours.

bios.title: Charlie Hane
paragraphs: Before going freelance full-time, Charlie was the Coordinator at Happy Accidents Media, helping oversee fifteen US and international productions with budgets ranging from $1-5 million, as well as the Asa Butterfield-led horror comedy show GNOMES. He reported directly to Executive Producers and Co-Founders Holly Hines (GINNY & GEORGIA, THE OFFICE) and Eric Jarboe (THE PRINCESS SWITCH). He associate produced the SAG-AFTRA series SWOLE MATE, a $250,000 production shot over fourteen straight days. Beyond producing, he has written film criticism for Bright Lights Film Journal, including a 2024 interview with ANORA's Palme d'Or and Academy Award-winning producer, Alex Coco.

bios.title: Charlie Hane
paragraphs: Charlie's filmmaking took root in high school, where his early films won multiple international and national awards. His first recognition came when 56 SWEET STREET took third place for Best Narrative Film at the Connecticut Cablevision Awards in 2014, and PRINCIPLES OF ROBBERY later won the 2017 Fritz Eager Award, the first film in nearly a decade added to his school's permanent art collection. That same summer, Northwestern's National High School Film & Video Institute picked him as one of ten directors; there, he directed, shot, and edited FIVE STRING, which won Outstanding Cinematography at the National New Age Film Festival. He then studied Film and Business at Syracuse University, but when the pandemic hit, he co-founded the Austin-based commercial videography company Voyager LLC, which cleared over $29,000 in profit in under six months and produced the $25,000 short film HALCYON DAYS. During that time he also wrote SHE'S A GOOD GIRL, which won Best Picture at the Texas 48 Hour Film Festival. Upon his return his junior year, he studied abroad at Prague's FAMU Film School, one of the world's top five film programs. While there, he was one of six chosen from twenty-three to direct a film, shooting on 35mm and leading a twenty-person production with a half-Czech crew and cast.
